lead: The ANC and DA opened formal coalition talks on Sunday amid reports the ANC wants to avoid a GNU-style pact in councils, while Ramaphosa heads to Silicon Valley. Markets brace for CPI on Wednesday and a SARB rate call on Thursday with the rand near R17/$.

items.title: ANC and DA open coalition talks as ANC weighs life without a council pact
items.summary: The two parties began formal talks on Sunday over hung municipalities, with no deal yet. Sources say the ANC NEC, backed by Ramaphosa, rejected a national GNU-style stability pact with the DA and is also courting MK, ActionSA, BOSA and the IFP.

items.title: Ramaphosa leads ministers on AI-focused Silicon Valley trip
items.summary: The president is in California from 15 to 21 November with the finance, trade, foreign affairs and communications ministers. The Presidency says the visit is about AI and is unrelated to the AGOA dispute with Washington.

items.title: Zuma Foundation disputes ConCourt refusal in R29m legal fees case
items.summary: The Constitutional Court declined to hear Jacob Zuma's appeal, leaving him liable to repay about R29 million in state-funded legal costs plus interest. His foundation says it respects the ruling but argues the state made the unlawful funding decision.

items.title: Phala Phala impeachment committee set to resume after court win
items.summary: The Western Cape High Court dismissed challenges to the committee's decision to drop its first choice of evidence leader. The committee, idle for over two months, may meet this week to pick a new nominee.

items.title: More than 77,000 Gauteng learners still without 2027 school places
items.summary: Of about 346,000 Grade 1 and 8 applications, some 268,000 have been placed and 278 schools are full. Pressure is highest in Ekurhuleni and Tshwane; the late application window opens on 17 December.

items.title: Small parties win a voice in hung eThekwini council
items.summary: The Ratepayers' movement ERPM took two PR seats, alongside one each for the PA, Minority Front and ACDP. No party reached the 112-seat majority, so coalition deals will decide who runs Durban.

items.title: Durban temples hit by string of thefts
items.summary: Temples in Umdloti, Verulam and elsewhere have lost aluminium windows, copper pipes, utensils and old brass statues. A temple chair says police should check scrapyards for stolen goods.

items.title: Tributes for Tongaat-born eNCA journalist Nabeelah Shaikh
items.summary: The award-winning investigative reporter, who began her career at the Sunday Tribune, died on Saturday from childbirth complications. Colleagues across the media paid tribute.

items.title: Iran fires drones at Bahrain, testing Gulf peace efforts
items.summary: Bahrain issued a nationwide alert and said it intercepted the attack; Iran's Guards claimed a hit on a US radar. Gulf states condemned it, and Iran's foreign minister is due in Muscat on Tuesday.

items.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East
items.summary: The USS Roosevelt joins two other carriers as the Iran war passes seven months, taking the US presence above 20,000 sailors and Marines.

items.title: COP31 enters final week with nations still far apart
items.summary: Over 7,000 people marched in Antalya at the talks' midpoint. Countries remain split on adaptation finance and fossil fuels ahead of the 20 November close.

items.title: Francophonie picks new leader amid Rwanda-DRC rift
items.summary: Leaders meeting in Cambodia choose a secretary-general on Monday. The DRC threatens to quit if Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo wins a third term and now backs Romania's Dacian Ciolos.

items.title: Cape Verde votes for president, with first female candidate
items.summary: Incumbent Jose Maria Neves is favoured against Joana Rosa among six candidates. A run-off follows on 29 November if nobody wins a majority.

items.title: South Sudan delays first national elections to February
items.summary: The vote moves from 22 December to 11 February 2027, at least the third postponement. Voter registration runs until 28 November.

items.title: Rand near R17/$ ahead of big week for rates
items.summary: The rand slid about 1.2% on Friday to around 16.98, its weakest since April, while the Top-40 fell 0.7%. October CPI is due Wednesday and the SARB decision Thursday.

items.title: Economists split on a SARB hike this Thursday
items.summary: The repo rate is 7.25% after September's hike. Nedbank expects another 25bp increase, while Investec and Old Mutual Wealth see rates on hold.

items.title: Early data points to petrol cut, diesel rise in December
items.summary: Preliminary CEF figures suggest 95 petrol could drop about R1.82/l, while diesel may rise over R1/l as temporary levy relief is scaled back on 2 December.

items.title: Boks edged 21-19 by France in Paris
items.summary: South Africa fought back from 21-7 down at half-time after a red card to Jasper Wiese. Rassie Erasmus blamed discipline and missed chances; Ireland are next.

items.title: Rabada takes 18th Test five-for but Bangladesh fight at Wanderers
items.summary: Hridoy hit 137 and Litton Das is 92 not out as Bangladesh closed day one on 327 for six.

items.title: Bafana held 2-2 by Kenya, return leg in Nairobi on Tuesday
items.summary: Benni McCarthy's Kenya equalised late in Johannesburg. Bafana stay top of their AFCON qualifying group ahead of the rematch at Nyayo Stadium.

items.title: Salah becomes Egypt's all-time top scorer
items.summary: Two goals in a 5-0 win over Malawi took him to 70 international goals, passing Hossam Hassan.

items.title: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage with tower arms
items.summary: On flight 15 the ship orbited 14 times, deployed 26 Starlinks and was caught at Starbase, though the booster did not return.
